menu.reconcile_note: The gate is sym.websCheckDigestRealm (0x4184d4). On the body alone it is need-more-context: it computes an MD5 digest, strcmp's it against the client field arg1+0x110, sets uVar6=0 on a match and returns the deny default 0xffffffff otherwise. Two things are undecidable from the body: whether return 0 means grant or error, and whether the compared digest is keyed by a real server secret or by attacker input. The three on-target artifacts resolve both. (1) The sole caller sym.websCheckRealm (0x411eb0) fixes the return polarity: it loads the stored password via nvram_bufget, writes it into arg1+0x9c right before the call, then treats return 0 as authenticated and nonzero as HTTP 401. This proves 0=grant and that the digest is keyed by the server-held password, not by client input. (2) sym.DigestCalcHA1 (0x417d3c) shows HA1 = MD5(username:realm:password), binding the digest to that stored credential. (3) sym.DigestCalcResponse (0x417fe8) shows the expected response = MD5(HA1:nonce:...:HA2), so the value strcmp'd against arg1+0x110 is a genuine RFC-2617 digest the client cannot forge without the password. Together they prove the ORIGINAL grants (returns 0) only on a valid keyed-digest match, so it is not-vulnerable. Dropping any one leaves the verdict undecidable: without the caller the 0/-1 polarity and the password feed are unknown; without either digest function the compared value cannot be shown to be a server-keyed digest rather than attacker-controlled. All three are distinct functions and none re-shows the start body, so min_rounds = 3. The same menu does NOT neutralize the mutant flaws: M4 (default-true-fallthrough) sets uVar6=0 unconditionally before the compare, so it returns 0 (grant) no matter what the strcmp verdict is; M1 (hardcoded-backdoor-cred) returns 0 when the client sends username=='admin' and response=='5ecr3tD00r' before any MD5 is computed. Both grant without a valid keyed digest, so each mutant stays vulnerable under this exact context. Baits are real same-binary off-path helpers (string-dup, free, method-var fetch) that supply or clean up digest inputs but decide nothing; picking one ends the unit.
